A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, including Appendices A–C, were readable, and the text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental and layout revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR100 experiments, NanoGPT perplexity results, and spectral and filtering analyses in Section 5, plus a training condition-number analysis in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR100 training/test errors, Crammed BERT filtering measurements and SuperGLUE results in Section 5, and retains the Appendix C analysis.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the nonsymmetric eigendecomposition but replaces signed-square eigenvalue parameterizations with clipping to [-1,0] or [0,1]. It removes the QR-based symmetric and half-sharpening variants and introduces a band-pass variant with paired positive/negative eigenvalues and a learnable epsilon. These change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: CIFAR100 remains, but ImageNet analyses, corrupted-image testing, and MiniPile/tiny Shakespeare perplexity evaluations disappear. v2 instead uses Pile masked-language-model training and SuperGLUE evaluations, covering CB, BoolQ, COPA, RTE, WiC, WSC, AX-g and MultiRC. This substantially changes the evaluated data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Centered Attention is added to the CIFAR100 performance comparison alongside the retained FeatScale baseline. Both also enter the eigenvalue and filtering comparisons that previously omitted them. The NLP comparison replaces NanoGPT with Crammed BERT, substantially revising the comparator framework.

E3.justification: CIFAR100 depths expand from 12/24 to 12/24/48, while the 10%/50% training-subset protocols are removed. NLP changes from a reduced NanoGPT trained for 10,000 iterations and evaluated by perplexity to 16/32-layer Crammed BERT, 24-hour masked-LM pretraining and task-specific fine-tuning evaluated by accuracy/F1. The stated CIFAR100 optimizer, 300 epochs and batch size 96 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the data-efficiency and 15-corruption/five-intensity robustness studies, the empirical symmetry analysis, and comparisons of symmetric, nonsymmetric and half-sharpening variants. It adds training-versus-test error analysis across depths and evaluation of the band-pass variant, while revising filtering analyses. Appendix C's condition-number analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both report uncertainty for CIFAR100: numerical ± estimates in v1 Tables 2–4 and graphical error bars in v2 Figure 5. NLP results remain point estimates. Neither explains the uncertainty statistic or provides run/seed counts. The display changes, but no substantive change in statistical reporting practice is established.

E6.justification: v1 Table 3 reports 12-layer ViT-Ti+ accuracy of 64.34% versus 66.78% for ViT-Ti; v2 Figure 5 reports test errors of 29.70% versus 31.29%, with revised parameterizations, and favors smoothing at 24/48 layers. Table 1 changes ViT-Ti's smoothing-dominant share from 98.92% to 73.99%. SuperGLUE scores replace perplexities, and scarcity/corruption results disappear. These are substantially revised results, not uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The filtering definition, fixed positive/invertible attention assumptions, spectral-dominance and feature-convergence results, rank-collapse corollaries, and Appendix A/B proofs are retained. v1 Theorems 1–4 correspond to v2 Theorems 3.3–3.5 and B.1; changes are numbering and typesetting rather than mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The central claim that Transformers are not inherently low-pass filters remains. However, the abstract replaces benefits from avoiding oversmoothing under scarce/corrupted data with task-dependent claims: smoothing helps image classification, while forced smoothing or sharpening hurts text generation. The introduction drops the majority-of-pretrained-models contribution, and the discussion identifies overfitting as the more important depth-scaling problem.

C2.justification: v1 explains sharpening as preserving useful information under scarcity/corruption and partial sharpening as preventing oversharpening. v2 interprets deeper vision results through overfitting and smoothing's generalization benefits, and argues that NLP needs more complex filtering. The theoretical limitations remain, including a now unsupported reference to benefits on the removed data-efficiency and corruption tests.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents He initialization for the eigenvector matrix and eigenvalue initialization with mean zero and standard deviation 0.1, including a stability rationale. NanoGPT configuration details are replaced by Cramming code-base guidance, a 24-hour budget, batch size 8192, sequence length 128, RTX 4090 hardware and bfloat16 training. QR implementation details disappear; the CIFAR100 recipe remains.

R1.justification: The core positioning against Dong et al., Wang et al. and graph-oversmoothing research remains. v2 adds Choi et al. and references supporting Cramming, SuperGLUE, initialization and efficient training, while removing citations associated with discarded experiments and parameterizations. The related-work argument itself changes only modestly.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, method explanation and Results narrative are substantially rewritten around filtering control. Training descriptions are reorganized into separate image and language accounts, Section 4 is retitled, and variant terminology and the discussion are revised. Background, theory and most appendix prose remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns with new typography and headers. Experimental tables are removed or replaced by grouped training/test-error and SuperGLUE bar charts; filtering plots receive revised panels, legends and layer-type markings. Figure 1 and the Appendix C condition-number curve remain, with the latter renumbered from Figure 6 to Figure 7.

improvement.justification: v2's training-versus-test error analysis, additional comparator and initialization guidance make the filtering/generalization investigation more informative. However, Section 7 retains data-efficiency and corruption claims after deleting their evidence, and prominent text-generation conclusions are supported by BERT/SuperGLUE understanding evaluations. These gains and claim-evidence mismatches leave the net change in overall quality unclear.
